scope: docs/r7-sql-repair-scope.md (7d8456b), committed before a line of the generator
P1_prime: every task has >= 1 SIBLING region — the symptom never pins its own region; tasks failing this are REJECTED at generation
k_varies: region counts 4 or 5 -> CHANCE IS PER TASK (20.0% or 25.0%), not v3 constant 20.4% — hazard 2 from the scope

CEILING_CHECK.why_generous: the model is handed the buggy query, the schema, and BOTH row counts; no inspection, no budget, no localisation. This BOUNDS the ceiling from above.
CEILING_CHECK.reading: 36.7% is far below the ~80% no-headroom line and far above zero. There IS room for a localisation prior. Hazard 3 from the scope does not fire.

THE_BUG_THIS_CHECK_CAUGHT_IN_ITSELF.cause: sqlite returns TUPLES; the task JSON round-trips rows to LISTS. The comparison could NEVER be true — the CLEAN query scored 0 too.
THE_BUG_THIS_CHECK_CAUGHT_IN_ITSELF.fix: normalise both sides, AND a POSITIVE CONTROL now runs first: the clean query must score as repaired on every task or no rate is printed at all.
THE_BUG_THIS_CHECK_CAUGHT_IN_ITSELF.lesson: the positive control is the cheapest check and I ran it second.

bounds: One seed (21), 300 tasks, sqlite in-memory with fixed fixture rows.
The ceiling is one-shot on 60 of the 300; the agent loop is not yet built.
A result-set verifier accepts ANY query returning the right rows — that is deliberate: two different queries can be equivalent and scoring on text would mark correct repairs wrong.
